No production source, consensus, authorization, storage, journal, crypto, accounting, manifest or workflow file is edited; no lifecycle predicate was changed, no private mutation interface was exposed, and the recovery requirement is NEVER cleared manually — it is cleared only by the ordinary public O5 API.

What is exercised (existing mechanisms only). The new tests DRIVE the pre-existing same-authority routes `fresh_vote_sign_real_local_same_authority` and `retained_vote_use_checked_same_authority_model` through the pre-existing public O2/O3/O5 barrier methods `SafetyRecordOwner::open` (O2 inspection), `read_validate` (O3 validation) and `reacknowledge` (O5 recovery), using the pre-existing `InjectFault` fault injection on the real backend. Every O2/O3/O5 call is made OUTSIDE any externally held safety-domain guard (these methods acquire their own guard); the protected-use routes keep their existing single-guard checking interval. No new protected-use implementation, classification API, or production mode parameter was introduced.

Coherent uncertain-publication fixture. A single shared helper `advance_engine_and_uncertain_durable_to_l1` keeps one backend incarnation, unchanged pinned context and authority, and the ORIGINAL captured envelope/Vote/pin (never rewritten or recaptured). It drives a GENUINE engine lock advance to the L1 successor through real `on_vote_event` quorum (peers 2 and 3), then publishes the corresponding SAME L1 successor restriction under `InjectFault::UncertainAfterWrite` via the existing `publish_locked`, asserting the EXACT `PublishResult::UncertainDurable` outcome and the resulting `recovery_required()` latch. The engine's actual lock, the surviving stored successor revision (established directly from the validated O3 proof, `publication_revision()==2`), the uncertain publication result, and the asserted recovery requirement are each established SEPARATELY — never inferred from an error or return label.

Fresh-signing recovery sequence (`same_authority_fresh_signing_recovers_through_o5_barrier`). (1) Before recovery: exact `RealFreshSignOutcome::ObservationRefused`, zero signer calls, zero sink calls, and no new D10 reservation (`reserved_position_count()==0`). (2) After successful O2 inspection and O3 validation but before O5: still `ObservationRefused` — inspection and validation do NOT clear the recovery requirement — and the held O3 proof's retained-holder reservation is observed raising BOTH the operational and aggregate ledgers above a proof-FREE baseline. (3) A successful O5 `reacknowledge(&proof)` → `PublishResult::DurableAcknowledged{new_revision:2}` clears the recovery requirement. The temporary O3 proof is DESTROYED (`drop`) before the proof-free comparison, and both ledgers are asserted restored exactly to the pre-proof baseline. (4) Re-entering the protected route re-runs observation, lifecycle, eligibility and authorization. (5) With coherent safe inputs: EXACTLY ONE real ML-DSA-44 signing call (2,420-byte signature), admitted publication, a separately reported `RetirementReport::Retired`, and the EXACT stored signature verified with `MlDsa44Backend::verify` against the UNCHANGED original Vote's journal-bound preimage under the authorized key. O5 is a storage recovery barrier, not signing authorization.

Checked retained-use recovery sequence (`same_authority_checked_retained_recovers_through_o5_barrier`). A genuine acknowledged `Signed` result is prepared through the real-signing model (one signer call) BEFORE the uncertain safety advance. Before O5 — including after successful O2/O3 — the checked route refuses (`ModelRetainedUseOutcome::ObservationRefused`) with zero sink calls, zero additional signer calls, and the existing `Signed` record byte-identical (verified by a direct bounded record read before/after). After successful O5 and fresh protected revalidation: checked retrieval, cryptographic verification, an EXACT retained-byte witness comparison through the RAII `RetainedSliceProbe` (one invocation, observed length 2420, matched true), and exactly one scalar sink call. The signer count stays 1 throughout the retained attempts. D10 retained-result acknowledgement requirements are kept SEPARATE from safety-record O5.

Failed and insufficient recovery controls. `o5_failed_recovery_variants_keep_recovery_and_block_dependent_use` loops over the three distinct O5 failure modes and asserts the EXACT result for each — `InjectFault::FailBeforeSubmit` → `RefusedPreWrite`, `WriteErrors` → `WriteFailedAmbiguous`, `UncertainAfterWrite` → `UncertainDurable` — each leaving the recovery requirement SET and both dependent fresh AND retained use refusing (a write error is NOT read as proof that no write occurred). Clearing the injected fault then demonstrates a successful ordinary-API O5 retry (`DurableAcknowledged{new_revision:2}`) that clears recovery. `cleared_recovery_with_wrong_engine_correspondence_still_refuses` is the insufficient-recovery control: O5 SUCCEEDS and clears the requirement, but the engine was deliberately NOT advanced (still locks L0) while durable advanced to L1; both dependent fresh and retained use STILL refuse at `ObservationRefused` — a cleared recovery requirement ALONE cannot authorize use.

Ownership, accounting and evidence. For the success and every exercised refusal, operational and aggregate baselines are read independently; complete borrowed-Vote equality and original pin provenance are preserved (`assert_cleanup_preserved`), exact cleanup is asserted with the envelope/pin still live, any O3 proof retained across O5 is accounted explicitly (proof-held baseline vs proof-free baseline distinguished, and the temporary proof destroyed before the proof-free comparison), and the existing ceilings are unchanged. This is fault-injected, IN-PROCESS evidence over real RocksDB safety storage, real ML-DSA-44 cryptography, and model journal/authority fixtures — kept DISTINCT from process-death or power-loss durability. It does NOT reconstruct prepared decisions after restart; across-process recovery remains separate.

## RUN 422 — Isolated Store-Reopen Recovery Boundary (clean close/reopen evidence)

Seven new test-only compositions were added inside `tests::real_fresh_sign` in `crates/qbind-node/src/safety_record_store/owner/model.rs`, demonstrating a genuine close/reopen of BOTH persistent backends — the safety-record RocksDB store and the signing-reservation RocksDB journal — each in its own retained `tempfile::tempdir()`. The reopen is a real release-then-reopen: incarnation A drops every owner/backend clone, journal handle and storage `Arc` that retains a RocksDB instance; incarnation B then succeeds with `SafetyRecordOwner::attach(open_enabled(dir), ..)` over the reopened safety directory and `SigningReservationJournal::open(RocksDbConsensusStorage::open(dir))` over the reopened journal directory (never the initialization fallback). A successful B reopen over the same directories proves the A RocksDB LOCK was released. This is CLEAN-REOPEN evidence with the harness deliberately retaining selected A objects to demonstrate their rejection; it is NOT process-death, power-loss, or production-restart acceptance. Engine reconstruction (`engine_locked_l0_multi_with_suite`) and all retained A objects are harness behavior.

Executed observations (this pass):
- `reopen_b_era_fresh_admitted_single_signer_single_sink` — A journal initialized with no reservation at the selected position; after B recovery (O2/O3/direct recovered-identity-vs-engine-lock comparison/O5/capture) the strict `fresh_vote_sign_real_local` path yields `Published` + `RetirementReport::Retired`: exactly 1 real signer call, 1 completion sink, durable-position count 0→1, stored 2,420-byte signature re-verified under the authorized key against the exact journal-bound preimage, and B's aggregate ledger returns to 0 after full teardown.

- `reopen_a_era_capability_refused_at_o5` — a genuine retained A O3 proof presented to B's `reacknowledge` is `RefusedPreWrite` by incarnation; durable revision unchanged, recovery still required, no standing charge added to B; the A proof's holder stays charged to A (verified by independent aggregate sampling) and only releases when dropped; a genuine B proof then recovers.

The existing journal holds its domain mutex across the callback (`signing_reservation_journal.rs:3515-3526`). Journal source then sets private `result_acked=true` only after the storage method returns and returns `Published` afterward (`signing_reservation_journal.rs:3707-3732`). Thus the child witnesses native synced-write success to the wrapper, not storage return to the journal, the private acknowledgement update, `Published`, or retirement. The latter three are excluded by the abort and established by source ordering, not by reading private state under lock. The model hook separately counts publication API entry immediately before the call and every return immediately after it (`owner/model.rs:3085-3087`).

**Submitted envelope, marker, and counters.** The source chain is admitted output’s borrowed `out.view()` → `publish_result_admitted`’s in-place `encode_signed_record_into` and framing → the wrapper’s actual borrowed framed envelope (`model.rs:3078-3087`; `signing_reservation_journal.rs:3560-3568, 3696-3708, 1097-1127`). The callback does not receive `AdmittedOutput`. The `R4W2` v1 phase `0x19` marker has exactly 4,211 bytes: magic `[0,4)`, version `[4,6)`, phase `[6,7)`, nonce `[7,23)`, eight little-endian `u32` counters `[23,55)` (boundary, signer, sink, publication entry, publication return, record attempt, delegated call, successful write), native-write ack `[55,56)`, wrapper-return flag `[56,57)`, suite `[57,59)`, key length/key `[59,61)/[61,1373)`, Vote length/Vote `[1373,1375)/[1375,1444)`, preimage length and 256-byte padded region `[1444,1446)/[1446,1702)`, actual key `[1702,1757)`, binding `[1757,1789)`, signature length `[1789,1791)`, and the actual submitted signature `[1791,4211)`. ### RUN 422 — isolated received-Vote evidence retention and invocation

The canonical `[u8; 32]` route now accepts an existing `VerifiedVoteToken` through one crate-private invocation. It validates the active context, epoch/roster, table and shared Bytes ledger before mutation; a refusal returns the same opaque token. After exactly one `HotStuffStateEngine::on_vote_detailed` call, it reconciles history and accumulator membership, then either transfers the original Vote, signature allocation, context handle and existing lease into a fixed table slot or destroys the token. The lease is reduced in place only after installation. No certificate is assembled or exposed, and no production caller is connected. A token proves signature validity under its installed context only; it proves no current authorization, transport authentication, durability, or publication permission.

The table owns 1,024 `Option<ReceivedVoteEvidenceEntry<BlockIdT>>` slots, allocated once using the checked `Layout::array` for that exact type and capacity. The shared ledger reserves the complete standing charge `S = size_of::<Option<ReceivedVoteEvidenceTable<BlockIdT>>>() + Layout::array::<Option<ReceivedVoteEvidenceEntry<BlockIdT>>>(1024).size()` before allocation, then commits that reservation only after all 1,024 slots initialize successfully. The defining-module layout test directly measured the private canonical types: `Vote=96/align 8`, `ReceivedVoteEvidenceEntry<[u8;32]>=160/align 8`, `Option<Entry>=160/align 8`, and `Option<Table>=48/align 8`; the actual allocator request is `163,840` bytes and `S=163,888` bytes. These compiler/target values are not stable ABI or allocator/RSS measurements. One private `Vec::from_raw_parts` transfer owns the exact global-allocation pointer as a zero-length Vec with matching fixed capacity; initialization tracks the live prefix and no growth or mutable Vec escape exists. Entry destruction precedes backing deallocation and the table lease release. Table staging precedes context adoption; allocation/budget refusals and a controlled pre-adoption unwind restore the existing ledger occupancy. A successful epoch/validator transition clears entries and context but retains table storage; `state_mut()` disables the producer and releases the whole table. A detached token keeps its own context and Bytes charge.

Evidence remains only while both `votes_by_view[(height, validator)]` maps to the logical block and the accumulator contains that signer for the same `(height, block)`. `Vote.height` is the logical view; signed round is preserved. The first evidence for a key is never replaced: exact duplicates, a different valid signature over identical signed fields, and conflicting signed fields are distinct dispositions. A new slot or key with missing evidence is refused before mutation when all slots are occupied; expected same-call evictions are not credited. Actual prior accumulator view eviction reconciles immediately and enables retry. The current zero-per-entry-limit behavior for an absent entry is preserved.

The table, wrapper, detached token/signature, and map-owned QC evidence use their applicable Bytes reservations under the shared byte cap. Active-context roster/key ownership retains the Context reservation class and context quota; a shared aggregate byte ceiling does not convert Context reservations into Bytes reservations. No second budget is introduced. On the measured x86_64 layout, `B=80`, one-member `C=1512`, active wrapper `W=32`, table `S=163888`, token inline control `T=128`, and test signature capacity `G=2420`. The observed equations are installation `B+C+W+S=165512`; admitted token `+T+G=168060`; retained transfer `B+C+W+S+G=167932`; entry removal returns to `B+C+W+S=165512`; epoch invalidation also releases active context/wrapper and returns to `B+S=163968`. Dropping an engine while a token remains detached releases `S` and the state owner but keeps `B+C+T+G=4140`; dropping the final token restores `B=80`. These are fixture/layout-specific ledger observations, not allocator or process-memory bounds.

Reconciliation is at the state mutation boundary: `on_vote_detailed` covers the legacy `on_leader_step` self-vote (`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs:3450`), shared Proposal self-vote (`:4091`), each restore/catch-up replayed signer (`:3312`), and each canonical token invocation. `on_leader_self_vote_detailed` covers the isolated owning-leader route (`:3063`) without changing its insertion early return; validator replacement clears stale memberships. Ordinary `on_vote` still attempts QC formation after duplicate/capacity-dropped accumulator results; the detailed leader path retains its distinct early return. State-level errors reconcile before the mutator returns. A legacy `on_vote_event` nonmember error after history mutation is an executed control (not an error reachable through a valid canonical token, whose preflight excludes a nonmember). That error skips Vote-event recorders and outer view advancement. The detailed isolated leader self-vote has a separate executed history-eviction/CapacityDropped control: it skips QC formation but reconciles and releases stale evidence before return. On success, evidence disposition precedes callbacks; a recorder panic propagates with ownership already coherent. Arbitrary generic Hash/Eq/Clone/destructor panic guarantees are not claimed.

The controlled membership-removal tests (`received_vote_reconciliation_requires_both_logical_memberships`) exercise independent helper-driven history/accumulator loss and establish the two-membership predicate; they are not return-path evidence. Separate `received_vote_legacy_state_error_reconciles_and_skips_event_callbacks` and `received_vote_leader_self_vote_capacity_drop_skips_qc_and_reconciles` tests now cause real history eviction and require entry removal before the actual Err/detailed-method return. The duplicate/conflict test captures the full expected Vote before first admission and after each disposition asserts complete ledger occupancy, unchanged cap, and byte-for-byte original Vote/signature pointer/capacity. Other allocation, ownership, refusal, retry, epoch cleanup, recorder-panic, and zero-limit controls remain as described below in the acceptance entry. Existing context/token/QC charges and caps are unchanged; installing the standing table charge `S` can make a previously affordable first context installation refuse.

This correction supersedes the earlier e71 return-path interpretation: its preservation-only assertions did not prove stale-entry reclamation. Starting branch `copilot/run-422-received-vote-retention`, HEAD `e71d02936539e51b60d9765d67162b0f866ef3c3`, root tree `00480e18b6a6aef4b31c3e9c8fe3e2e1a134b51a`. The historical D7 blob from integrated baseline `1dcf63a0669aacf98fa61ca1e9c654219a36450c` (`767ee6bf877b827aa27d9c48eafbfdec86c35b63`) is preserved as the exact byte prefix; the relocated retention section, preserved prior acceptance entry, and this final acceptance correction follow it. Production behavior, allocation, ownership, ledger formulas, and outcomes are unchanged.

**Return-path evidence.** The legacy nonmember error test now constructs `BasicHotStuffEngine::with_state_limits` with `max_votes_by_view_entries=1`, installs the context/table, and retains the actual signed validator-0 Vote at its logical `vote.height`. Before the error it verifies the first history and accumulator memberships, retained entry, and complete ledger tuple `(B+S+C+W+G, pending=0, contexts=1, pending_contexts=0)`. The existing `on_vote_event(ValidatorId(99), &vote)` path inserts validator 99 into history and returns `NonMemberSigner`; with the limit one, that history insertion evicts validator 0 while the accumulator still contains validator 0. On return the test requires validator 99 history present, validator 0 history absent, accumulator count still one, table entry absent, and exact postcondition `(B+S+C+W, 0, 1, 0)`: precisely signature-capacity G released, while standing table S, active context C, wrapper W, and the context count remain. It also checks pending bytes, cap unchanged, zero callbacks, and unchanged outer view. No explicit reconciliation call is made. This is a legacy error control only; the nonmember error is not claimed reachable from a valid canonical token.

The detailed leader self-vote test uses the two-validator fixture with `max_votes_per_view=1` and `max_votes_by_view_entries=1`. Validator 0's admitted/signed Vote is retained first, with history+accumulator memberships and exact ledger `(B+S+C+W+G, 0, 1, 0)`. Invoking `on_leader_self_vote_detailed(ValidatorId(1), same_view, same_block)` inserts validator 1 into history, evicts validator 0's history membership, leaves validator 0 in the accumulator, and reports `CapacityDropped` for validator 1. QC-attempt count is unchanged and the detailed report says QC was not processed/formed. Before return the old evidence entry is gone and ledger is `(B+S+C+W, 0, 1, 0)`, with only G released and cap unchanged. The separate helper-driven membership-removal test remains a predicate control, not the basis for either return-path claim.

**Duplicate/conflict evidence.** `received_vote_token_invocation_transfers_original_and_keeps_first_evidence` now captures the expected complete signed Vote before first admission. Its existing pre-shrink instrumentation still observes the original signature pointer/capacity installed in the table while the full token-inline-plus-signature lease is attached. After exact duplicate, distinct valid signature over identical signed fields, same-key signed-field conflict, and different-block equivocation, each assertion compares the first entry against the pre-invocation Vote using redacted Boolean equality, checks the original signature pointer/capacity, compares the full occupancy tuple `(committed_bytes, pending_bytes, committed_contexts, pending_contexts)` to the retained baseline, and verifies the byte cap is unchanged. Signed height and round remain independently asserted.

**Source paths versus executed routes.** Source inspection establishes `on_vote_detailed` beneath legacy self-vote, shared Proposal self-vote, each restore/catch-up replayed signer, and canonical token invocation; validator replacement clears both logical memberships then reconciles. The isolated detailed leader route is also source-established and now has the direct executed eviction control above. The new tests execute the legacy `on_vote_event` error return and isolated detailed leader early return, and the token invocation duplicate path. Controlled membership removal remains helper-driven. Shared-Proposal and restore/catch-up outer routes have not been newly executed as retention integration tests; no route coverage beyond the named tests is claimed.

## RUN 422 — Isolated received-Vote signed-QC staging (implemented, not independently accepted)

This entry supersedes the preceding "No certificate assembly" statement only for the isolated
received-Vote route described here. Starting baseline was `0525f772d11c0c67ce509fa43b8283f87bb39eb4`
(`ecd0feac98c6d45fd66668d84ccde3fb863d211d` root tree), verified as the checkout HEAD/tree with a clean
worktree; content correspondence and commit ancestry were checked separately. Work is confined to the
six authorized paths. The implementation is opt-in and has no production caller, O4 connection, current
authority, signing/delivery, activation, deployment, D15, or Run 423 surface.

`VoteAccumulatorProjection` is bound by borrow to the accumulator, incoming voter, view, and block;
the same insertion classifier drives projection and mutation. It remains non-`Clone`/non-`Copy`, and the
borrow ends before mutation. The route then carries its private candidate seal without an intervening
mutation or callback into exactly one `on_vote_detailed` call. The fixed `[u64; 16]` witness is filled
from the pre-event projection with checked dense-roster bounds, retained through reconciliation, and
compared against the actual QC by candidate, count, range, uniqueness, and exact membership. Evidence is
copied before mutation in ascending validator order; the lowest-index selected retained Vote anchors the
eight common signed fields. Existing evidence wins over a conflicting incoming duplicate, and only an
absent selected incoming entry under `NewEntry` may use the token. Height maps to logical view; signed
round is preserved. Missing/incompatible evidence yields Incomplete, never a partial certificate.

The complete certificate is a plain wire QC with exact original signature bytes, minimal bitmap span,
ascending signature-vector order, and a source-context handle in every invoked report. It is not a
`VerifiedQuorumCertificate`, current authorization, publication permission, or durable acknowledgement.
`NoQc`, `Incomplete`, `LogicalError`, and `Complete` remain distinct. The event summary preserves history,
accumulator disposition (including skipped equivocation), evidence disposition, QC summary, and view
advancement. Reconciliation and callbacks remain on the existing one-invocation path and retain their
ordering/panic behavior.

**Measured ownership contract (x86_64 test target).** Report-class A is reserved before stage controls
or destination buffers are built:

```
A = checked_add(size_of::<ReceivedVoteQcRouteControlFrame>(),
                max(size_of::<QcAdmissionControlFrame>(),
                    size_of::<QcBufferBuildFrame>()))
  = 1816 + max(216, 1032) = 2848 bytes
```

The route frame inventory is token/preflight, report/context owner, bound projection, candidate seal and
membership witness, control-charge result, staged wire/result, logical mutation report, event summary,
final outcome, refusal, and return `Result` carrier. The admission frame includes budget clone/result,
pending/report reservation and commit result, temporary committed report lease, context clone result,
report owner and return result. The buffer frame includes source refs; common fields and scan/layout
scalars; allocation and push results; partial bitmap, descriptor, and signature `ExactBuffer`s; transferred
Vecs; pending P reservation and commit result; logical wire-QC, wire owner, and preparation result.
The nested admission and buffer helpers are lifetime-disjoint; their maximum is added to the persistent
route frame. The route layout conservatively includes controls such as the incoming token that are also
covered by its pre-existing Bytes-class token charge; this is intentional extra frame coverage, not a
claim that the token payload charge was subtracted. These are component ownership bounds, not stack/RSS
or allocator-overhead claims.

For `n` selected signers and highest selected validator id `h`, complete preparation reserves
`P = (h / 8 + 1) + n * size_of::<Vec<u8>>() + n * ML_DSA_44_SIGNATURE_SIZE`; every backing allocation
uses the corresponding exact capacity and initialized length. On the measured target, three signers
produce `P=1+72+7260=7333`; four produce `P=1+96+9680=9777`. A known-incomplete or equivocation
preparation has `P=0`; prevalidation returns before any destination allocation. A candidate prepared
before an actual `NoQc` is discarded and releases P before report return. Complete reports retain P;
incomplete/no-QC reports retain no P. The report quota is committed separately from table capacity.
On the three/four-signer route observations, A was 2848 bytes per report, P was respectively 7333/9777,
pending bytes and pending contexts returned to zero, and report/context counts returned to baseline when
the report was dropped.

The inherited logical QC allocation produced by the engine's existing accumulator is outside this new
staging budget; it is inspected, summarized, and dropped rather than retained by the report. Source Vote
signature capacity, table, installed context, token, and ledger charges remain owned by their existing
components. Drop order is destination backing before P lease, report outcome/backing and source context
before A lease.

This append supersedes the accounting stop as the current implementation/test
result; the stop above remains historical evidence and is not rewritten. Source

**Exact candidate ownership.** `owner/received_qc_publication_model.rs`
implements a private, test-only exact-copy owner, reachable only through
`#[cfg(all(test, feature = "test-utils"))]`. Allocation-free
`validate_candidate_shape` first checks the QC scalar/domain correspondence,
logical signer uniqueness, bitmap correspondence, bounded counts and source
capacities. `CandidateCopyPlan` uses checked `Layout::array`, checked byte
arithmetic, nonzero/isize bounds and the exact source lengths. Workspace
reservation precedes candidate reservation; both precede the first
destination allocation. The existing authoritative load completes and its
proof is destroyed before candidate construction.

`ExactBuffer<T>` owns the exact global-allocator pointer/layout immediately,
tracks its initialized prefix, and releases only that prefix before deallocation.
Each in-flight signature has its own guard until it transfers into the
initialized descriptor prefix. A completed buffer transfers to `Vec` only with
the original pointer, matching array layout, initialized length and exact
capacity. Null allocation, layout, admission, shape and injected-allocation
outcomes remain distinct. O4 receives the entire candidate through unchanged
`publish_locked_held`; candidate and workspace leases remain alive until O4 has
destroyed the moved candidate on every result. Borrowed source QC/report bytes,
capacities and pointers are not mutated.

The compiler-derived candidate control inventory is 849 bytes in a 1,024-byte
workspace; the separately measured exact local-Vote copy inventory is 536
bytes in its own 1,024-byte workspace. Observed constituent layouts include
candidate owner 704, plan 112, exact buffer 40, allocation result 16 and
`LockedRecord` 360 bytes. The compile-time bounds and executable assertions
both pass. Three-signature candidate backing is exactly
`360 + 1 + 3*(24 + 2420) = 7693` bytes. A valid four-signature candidate keeps
all signatures and requires 10,137 bytes; under the full interrupted-O4

The exact local Vote uses a separately admitted workspace and candidate charge

### Run 422 bounded signed-QC ownership and acceptance correction

**Starting revision and scope.** The checkout was clean on
`copilot/run-422-received-vote-signed-qc-staging` at
`d6e8bdb61173ff4fb3c8a454911da9dd45a3b0f3`, root tree
`1870829eb5b10fa633926e2e326002deedf0c8e0`. This correction changes only
`basic_hotstuff_engine.rs`, `received_vote_evidence.rs`, and the two authorized evidence documents.
Earlier validation and the 2848-byte A measurement above remain historical evidence for their producing
source revision; they are not results for this correction.

**Backing-before-reservation cleanup.** `ReceivedVoteQcReportOwner::build_wire` now matches the complete
commit Result. On refusal it retains the returned valid `PendingCharge`, explicitly destroys the
complete wire QC (including nested signature/descriptor/bitmap backing), then releases that reservation.
Typed refusal returns the original token without logical invocation or callbacks. The scoped test-only
commit fault returns the untouched valid reservation before the ledger commit, without modifying ledger
state or relaxing production invariants. It exercises the real error-cleanup branch; it is
defensive-error-path evidence, not an observed production exploit or reachable ordinary `on_qc` error.
Observations immediately before and after QC destruction retain the same full pending P; a third
observation records pending P becoming zero only after cancellation.

**Opaque returned owner.** `ReceivedVoteQcReport` is defined in a private child module with private
actual/outcome/provenance fields. Its route-only constructor transfers all owners together. Callers and
tests inspect `actual()` and `outcome()` through shared borrows; there is no mutable accessor or
owned-outcome extraction. Field destruction order remains actual summary, outcome/QC backing and P,
source context, then Report-class A. Thus the QC backing cannot be moved out of a returned report while
discarding its required provenance/A. This remains a plain wire QC with historical provenance, not a
verified/current-authority capability.

**Reconciled compiler-derived inventory (x86_64).**

```
A = checked_add(size_of::<ReceivedVoteQcRouteControlFrame>(),
                max(size_of::<QcAdmissionControlFrame>(),
                    size_of::<QcBufferBuildFrame>()))
  = 2096 + max(288, 1600)
  = 3696 bytes, Report class, one report-quota slot
```

| Inventory | Simultaneously covered controls and conservative overlap |
|---|---|
| Persistent route, 2096 B | Complete token/preflight, Report/context owner, bound projection, fixed candidate/membership seal, stage/result/wire controls, logical mutation result and moved logical QC, saved incomplete reason, event/QC summaries, outcome, report/refusal/full return carrier, candidate/cursor/count/boolean scalars. Source and destination report-constructor controls are both covered. |

### Run 422 isolated received-QC effect gate

**Baseline and scope.** The clean starting checkout was content-equal to, but not descended from,
the required `dc782786a4c477295f6be5e567d5c45740b89698`. That pinned object was fetched and verified
separately: root tree `f486d8ce00a277c0ae83767c3d984592c68d8512`, parent
`0525f772d11c0c67ce509fa43b8283f87bb39eb4`. The new
`copilot/run-422-received-qc-effect-gate` branch was created from the exact pinned commit before
editing. Equal content with the prior local correction commit did not establish ancestry or justify
substituting that commit. Changes are confined to Basic/state-engine Rust modules and these two
evidence documents; the received-Vote ownership foundation is reused unchanged.

**Source-established ordering.** `HotStuffStateEngine::ingest_vote_and_form_qc` now holds the one
shared history/accumulator/QC-formation path. Existing `on_vote_detailed` still applies every formed
QC and then reconciles evidence. Its opt-in sibling `on_vote_detailed_effect_gated` instead reconciles
completed bookkeeping first, consults the adapter for every actual QC, and calls `on_qc` only on
allowance. There is no lock-view shortcut: duplicate, equal-view, and lower-view QCs all encounter
the seam. No completed-route replay, rollback, second accumulator, or duplicate callback path exists.
Ordinary duplicate/capacity-drop QC attempts and the separate leader self-vote policy are unchanged.

Basic's `invoke_verified_received_vote_qc_effect_gated` shares pre-mutation staging with the existing
signed-QC route. Before the caller gate, `ReceivedQcGateAdapter` checks actual block/view, signer
count, index bounds, uniqueness, and full projected membership. Only complete corresponding signed
evidence reaches `ReceivedQcEffectGate::evaluate`. Missing/mixed evidence or correspondence failure
suppresses application while retaining the honest logical-QC summary. NoQc, equivocation, and
logical errors do not invoke the gate. First-retained original signatures and all signed fields,
including round independent of logical height/view, remain authoritative.

The private-constructed `ReceivedQcEffectView` borrows the actual logical QC and staged plain wire
QC. It exposes explicit optional pre-application lock identity, target own-QC, committed block/height,
borrowed commit log, and current Basic view for narrow boundary observations. It gives no mutable
engine access, owned-QC extraction, verified-QC capability, or current authorization. The caller owns
the borrowed gate and its arbitrary implementation/storage. `Allow` is an isolated decision, not a
durable acknowledgement, publication/release permission, or signing/delivery authorization.

`ReceivedVoteQcEventSummary.application` separates Ungated, NotAttempted, Suppressed(reason),
Refused(reason), and Attempted(actual processing result). Complete signed evidence does not imply
application success. `on_qc` still returns success on its ordinary source-established paths; the
typed attempted-error carrier is future defensive representation, not an observed reachable failure.
Refusal/suppression preserves lock, target own-QC, committed block/height, commit log, and QC-driven
view state. Ordinary Vote/equivocation notifications retain their existing once-only behavior; no
QC-success/view-advance callback runs on refusal/suppression. Allowance preserves successful callback
ordering. Vote history/accumulator bookkeeping is not rolled back and the consumed token is not
returned as unconsumed.

**Ownership and accounting.** The report remains an opaque owner with borrowed `actual()` and
`outcome()` only; context, Report quota/A, and QC backing/P cannot be independently extracted.
Backing-before-lease destruction and the earlier defensive commit-refusal cleanup remain unchanged.
Reconciliation now precedes the fallible/panicking gate boundary. A gate panic therefore leaves
completed logical bookkeeping but reclaims history-evicted source evidence, drops staging and the
incoming token, applies no QC effects, runs no later callbacks, and returns no successful report.
The later QC-callback-panic case instead preserves already applied QC/commit effects and retained
incoming evidence while releasing staging. Neither case claims transaction rollback.

Compiler-evaluated x86_64 controls now measure:

```
route = 2168 B; admission = 288 B; buffer = 1600 B; gate = 832 B
A = checked_add(route, max(admission, buffer), gate) = 4600 B
P = minimal bitmap + exact signature Vec descriptors + exact original signature allocations
P(3 signers) = 7333 B; P(4 signers) = 9777 B
```

`ReceivedQcGateControlFrame` inventories the borrowed gate, embedded adapter, adapter/state-gate/state
borrows, input and by-value input argument controls, logical-QC borrow, application and return
carriers, state/route tuple results, lock summary, incomplete reason, decision, and bool return.
The route frame compiler-sizes the enlarged summary/report/result carriers. The frame sum is
conservative across some disjoint lifetimes; embedded adapter/borrowed input fields are not charged
as separate heap allocations. Existing full token-control coverage is retained conservatively.
Actual byte/descriptor push-result types and nested cleanup controls remain in the accepted buffer
inventory. The shared staging route uses the revised A; nongated logical/callback behavior is
unchanged. No additional ledger, quota, generic reference-counting framework, or owned callback
budget was introduced.

A/Report admission precedes staging allocation and ingestion; destination P admission precedes all
bitmap/descriptor/signature allocations. During staging, source ownership, A, and reserved P overlap;
after P commit, complete backing retains its lease through gate execution/report lifetime. The
returned owner retains A and context for every invoked outcome; P survives only with complete
backing. The existing separate report quota is not evidence-table capacity. Gate inputs borrow
inherited backing; engine logical-QC/signer allocations, lock/block-QC clones, and commit-log storage
remain inherited engine allocations outside this new component bound. This is not an RSS bound.

Executed regression observations: detached three-signer report tuple `(17581,0,1,0,1,0)`,
four-signer tuple `(20025,0,1,0,1,0)`, and independent final baseline `(80,0,0,0,0,0)`.
Tuples mean committed bytes, pending bytes, committed contexts, pending contexts, committed reports,

token charge minus two evicted signature charges, with zero pending/report counts. Final teardown
independently restores the empty-ledger baseline. Earlier A=3696 observations and validation remain
historical, attributed to their producing revision rather than relabeled here.

## RUN 422 - isolated received-QC / O4 acknowledgement / QC-effect composition

**Producing source revision:** `12c39541bd00f93f5e9cf7e8940ec7c5c13ec7ff`;
root tree `387174be19432615115ed99f2e1540b6c7cee1aa`.
The starting main was exactly `00a73da0fb30d50478b2b462d902f85323944e54`,
tree `73626cfea1365f52e1776e31c631a8af09875af7`. The worktree was clean;
commit availability (`cat-file`), exact tree correspondence (`rev-parse`), and
ancestry (`merge-base --is-ancestor`) were checked separately. No baseline fetch
or substitution was needed. Work is confined to `copilot/run-422-received-qc-o4-model`.

**Implemented, isolated only.** An opt-in consensus `test-utils` facade beneath
`basic_hotstuff_engine` executes the accepted private admission, original-token
retention, complete wire-QC staging, and pre-`on_qc` effect-gated route. Node's
existing feature forwards this feature; its composition module is private and
requires BOTH `test` and `test-utils`. Tokens, evidence internals, and gate/report
implementation remain crate-private. Reports retain their original ownership
and destruction contract; wire inspection is borrowed, not an extracted clone.
There is no unchecked token constructor, mutable context access, raw ledger
mutation, fabricated verified certificate, duplicate ingestion, or manual
`on_qc` invocation.

`publish_locked` is now a thin domain-locking wrapper around its one private
held-guard body. The body retains the existing preflight, revision fence,
authoritative predecessor validation, strictly increasing lock rule, accounting,
publication results, and effectiveness transition. The model acquires that SAME
domain once before the consensus invocation, checks the immutable context and
authoritative charged loader result, calls ordinary O4 without re-acquiring the
domain, and holds it through gate return, QC application, success callbacks,
and synchronous route return. Only the actual `DurableAcknowledged` return maps
to Allow. A post-ack/pre-effective hook observes zero new QC applications and
QC/view success callbacks; a competing thread's nonblocking acquisition reports
WouldBlock over a bounded channel (5-second failure deadline, no sleep).
Synchronous ordinary callbacks also observe contention; acquisition succeeds
after return. These callbacks never invoke owner operations re-entrantly.

**Authority assumption, not current-authority integration.** An independently
constructed immutable fixture has four dense validators, power 1 each, genuine
suite-100 ML-DSA-44 keys and 2420-byte signatures. Its commitment hashes runtime
chain, wire chain 7, genesis, epoch 0, indices, powers, suite and length-prefixed
public keys. Both the actual admission snapshot and pinned storage context derive
from it. Borrowed snapshot inspection checks the domain, epoch, suite, exact
membership/power/keys and key shape; the node checks pinned genesis, authority
reference, chain, epoch, suites, signature size and storage profile. Shared epoch
or count alone is insufficient. This fixture does NOT establish production
current authority.

The candidate uses the actual gate-supplied logical identity and complete staged
wire certificate, including every original signature and signed wire field.
Logical view binds wire height; wire round remains 9, not height. A genuinely
admitted duplicate signed with round 19 uses the FIRST retained round-9 evidence.
Under the held domain, the existing charged loader validates stored content and
independent history; expected revision and exact engine/storage lock identity
must agree, including honest bootstrap absence. Equal/lower candidates refuse
before O4. The caller-owned candidate is reserved before its copy. Ordinary O4
recomputes the evidence binding and validates it. Existing committed anchors are
preserved and require independent history; an anchor is NOT inferred from a
commit that the later `on_qc` will produce. In this registered-chain fixture the
first committed grandparent has actual height 0, not a coerced absent anchor.
Storage stage-2 verification remains unwired and readback remains `Unverified`.
Domain-aware cryptographic verification in these tests is TEST EVIDENCE only.

### Ownership inventory and phase bounds (64-bit, N=4/S_sig=2420)

The source inventory in `adapter_charge`, `candidate_charge` and facade
`control_bytes` precedes all adapter/candidate copies and uses existing
`Reservation` ownership patterns; it is not a new allocator or refcount system.
All returned diagnostics are bounded scalars. Field order destroys the opaque
report before node coverage; the report's existing backing/context/report-owner
drop order is unchanged. Loader objects/scratch use the existing charged
held-guard loader, are destroyed before candidate copying, and remain covered
while live. The caller's candidate lease persists across O4's independent
working-set reservation, including refusal and unwind.

#### Run 422 F5 — mandatory Timeout/NewView verification

The executable P2P consensus preflight now selects `TimeoutVerificationPolicy::RequireOrFail` regardless of whether `--require-timeout-verification` is supplied. The flag remains accepted for CLI compatibility and cannot opt into optional verification. P2P startup refuses before P2P service construction when a validated `TimeoutVerificationContext` cannot be assembled. LocalMesh and other non-consensus CLI operations remain available, while their direct Timeout/NewView handler boundaries reject absent verification context. The local timeout timer is independently disableable; authenticated inbound Timeout/NewView processing remains active and still reaches origin and verification admission.

The runtime handler continues to apply authenticated-origin binding and bounded decoding before requiring context. Inbound Timeout frames are admitted only after `verify_timeout_msg`; inbound NewView frames are admitted only after `verify_timeout_certificate_with_evidence` validates the exact certificate and its complete signed-timeout evidence. Local timeout emission checks context, signer identity, governed suite, and verifier backend before constructing or ingesting a message; it self-verifies the signed Timeout before local ingestion and broadcast. A locally formed TC is verified against its exact `signed_timeouts` before engine application or NewView broadcast, both when an inbound timeout completes quorum and when a local timeout completes quorum. Missing signing prerequisites do not consume the per-view latch or increase backoff. No Proposal/Vote authority or timeout signing-reservation journal integration was added; Timeout signing positions remain outside the Proposal/Vote signing contract.

Focused evidence uses real ML-DSA-44 signatures and the executable startup boundary. `run030` selected 24 tests, the timeout verification bridge selected 20, and `run422_mandatory_timeout` selected 2; all passed with `test-utils`. The complete `qbind-node` library suite passed 2180 tests (6 ignored). The mandatory policy startup target passed 2 tests, including no-flag P2P refusal for the signer/context reason and non-consensus genesis-hash operation. Directly affected integration targets passed: authenticated-origin/timer-disabled demux 4, authenticated sender binding 18, D4 P2P startup ordering 5, genesis-authority preservation 15, Run 420 production policy 3, and startup refusal 4. `cargo build --locked -p qbind-node` and CRLF-aware `git diff --check` passed.

#### Run 422 F5 acceptance-evidence follow-up

The default-feature unit-test compile defect was a pre-existing test-configuration mismatch, not a production F5 vulnerability: the lifecycle helpers/tests and their references to `received_qc_publication_model` and `received_qc_effect_test_support` were present at the pre-F5 baseline `56763bd14cdc21b88b76a0aa19218f037ed2f4a4`, while those support APIs require `test-utils`. Only the directly dependent lifecycle helpers and tests in `owner/model.rs` are now feature-gated. The lifecycle tests remain executable with `--features test-utils`; production dependencies, owner implementation, and accounting are unchanged. The earlier paragraph in this evidence document saying default-feature selectors do not compile is historical for the pre-fix source, not the current state; all three default-feature selectors and the default-target compilation command below now pass.

The new refusal test uses an enabled, unsaturated pacer (`base=1`, multiplier `2`, cap `8`) and compares its threshold, level, increase/reset/cap-hit counters, timeout-window state, engine view/lock/latch, timeout accumulator, and outbound count around missing-context, missing-signer, signer-error, and successful-signing/wrong-key self-verification refusals. It then restores the valid signer and retries on that same state. The wrong-key signer uses a genuine ML-DSA-44 keypair and call counters prove signing returned success before configured-key verification rejected it; no key bytes or signatures are logged. A private-helper-level locally formed TC test rejects malformed cryptographic evidence before view/lock or NewView effects and pairs that with valid evidence acceptance. It is not a network-reachable attack demonstration. Existing positive B14 tests continue to exercise inbound-timeout quorum completion and local-timeout quorum completion. Timeout-evidence verification does not establish verification of logical `high_qc` constituent Votes, current-authority freshness, or O4 publication.

The bounded subprocess target now supervises both P2P startup and the genesis-hash operation, captures at most 128 KiB per output stream, and kills/reaps owned children on timeout or unwinding. Its no-compatibility-flag positive control uses isolated loopback configuration and a valid temporary ML-DSA-44 signer/key pair. Observing `timeout verification ACTIVE` proves real P2P preflight acceptance only; it does not claim the later P2P transport readiness marker or a running transport.

#### Run 422 startup marker exit-race correction

`SupervisedChild::wait_for_stderr_marker` now takes a final stderr snapshot after `observe_exit()` joins the output readers. If that completed capture contains the requested marker, the wait succeeds; otherwise `UnexpectedEof` reports that same final snapshot. This closes the exit/read-drain ordering gap while retaining the bounded deadline, capture cap, child ownership, and distinction between ACTIVE preflight acceptance and transport readiness. #### Run 422 F7 — bounded retained-QC admission

Implemented on source commit `d17a4db2a24c682f988594e6c3347f24adeffcae`.
F5 mandatory outer-timeout verification and the checked TC target-view
relationship are preserved. Inbound Timeout, inbound NewView, local timeout,
and locally formed TC/NewView now gate every present logical high-QC before
accumulator insertion/eviction, lock/view/latch changes, or TC application and
publication. `None` remains a separate no-QC case; `Some([0; 32], view 0)`
requires retained proof. TimeoutVerificationContext remains limited to timeout
authentication and is never Proposal/Vote authority. Production currently has
no admitted Proposal/Vote snapshot, so present-QC claims fail closed; positive
controls use test-only snapshots and genuine constituent signatures.

The read-only lookup scans child blocks' retained verified justifications,
matching the actual logical projection: block ID, logical view to wire QC
height (never round), and exact ascending signer identities. Reordered or
duplicate signer lists do not match. Identical complete certificates on
multiple children are one candidate; distinct complete certificates with the
same projection return typed ambiguity. The scan refuses a tree larger than
`min(configured max_pending_blocks, 4096)` before iteration. It allocates no
candidate collection, clones no evidence, and does not change evidence,
accounting, or eviction state. Missing and evicted proof are the same fail-closed
admission result.

Present-QC admission uses only the supplied snapshot's bound verifier for
domain, epoch, membership, keys, and backend; it checks engine epoch/weights and
timeout-context chain/membership correspondence before QC cryptography, then
reverifies the complete retained wire certificate through the shared verifier
core and confirms the original ticket immediately before effect. The private
guard binds the exact borrowed claim, timeout context, snapshot, operation, and
ticket. Runtime calls are synchronous; those borrowed inputs are immutable,
engine-mutating callbacks are not handed to verification/signing, and the local
timeout path reconfirms the original ticket after signing and immediately
before ingestion. TC application performs its own admission of the actually
selected QC; prior timeout admission is not reused as proof.
On local refusal, the pre-existing progress observation remains an observation
only; F7 does not consume the timeout latch, insert into the timeout
accumulator, or advance timeout backoff.

The enforced F7 component ceiling is 1 MiB per present-QC operation, checked
with overflow-safe arithmetic before revalidation. It charges the selected
retained evidence's capacity accounting (within the existing 256 MiB evidence
ledger), decoded Timeout/TC inline storage and nested vector capacities,
one-at-a-time per-Vote `Vote`/signature temporary, canonical Vote body plus
overlapping v2 preimage, the borrowed verifier's fixed result storage, and the
operation guard. Borrowed revalidation shares the existing QC crypto core but
creates neither a signer-vector allocation nor an owned certificate result;
therefore there is no returned certificate backing to charge. The encoded
inbound frame is released immediately after bounded decode to avoid overlapping
it with the decoded control object. Key-provider/backend internal work and
backend-produced error strings are inherited and not included in this F7
component ceiling; allocator metadata/rounding, fragmentation, stack/process
memory, unrelated retained engine state, and physical memory/RSS are also not
bounded or claimed. No RSS measurement was performed.

Timeout signing preimages are unchanged. The existing encoding maps `None` to
zero block ID/view, so `None` and `Some(zero block ID, view 0)` remain
signing-preimage-ambiguous; F7 does not reinterpret or normalize that claim.
Unknown remote QCs, cold starts, evicted evidence, unavailable/superseded
authority, and over-limit state therefore fail closed. This slice adds no
wire-carried proofs, production authority activation/currentness, O4
publication, restart safety, or complete F7/RS1 closure. No deployment,
trust-anchor selection, D15, or Run 423 is implied.

#### Run 422 F7 — accounting and handler acceptance reconciliation

Finishing-pass source revision:
`efa76f08134792d754a0a25fae7898df6579592e`. The starting task branch was

`18b4e8d8db03a481bb73eee6af2d3d32c065634e` was an ancestor. The retained
lookup and four runtime gate placements are unchanged. Only the node
accounting/helper tests and QC verifier's fixed accounting constant changed;
the shared cryptographic verification algorithm is unchanged.

This reconciles the preceding accounting claim: 1 MiB is an enforced,
checked, named-component envelope for synchronous admission/revalidation and
its return transfers, NOT a whole-handler or physical-memory bound. The
production wrapper still supplies exactly 1,048,576 bytes; the internal
calculation clamps any supplied budget to that ceiling. Tests lower the budget
through the same production calculation, with real capacity-bearing inputs.
No runtime setting, generic allocator, wire/preimage change, or enlarged
existing ceiling was added.

The phase inventory in `f7_qc_working_set` is:

| Phase / component | Charged ownership and backing |
|---|---|
| Selected source (R) | `retained_byte_size()` of the engine-selected evidence: complete certificate, bitmap, outer signature-vector capacity, each signature capacity, and retained signer-vector capacity. It remains covered by the existing retained ledger; including R in this smaller operation envelope is not a second reservation or a larger ledger allowance. |
| Actual input (C) | Timeout inline size plus signature capacity and logical-QC signer capacity; or TC inline size, TC signer/high-QC backing, signed-timeout vector capacity times Timeout inline size, and each live nested signature/QC-signer capacity. Inline parent slots already include their nested QC and Vec descriptors, so those descriptors are not added a second time. |
| Reconstructed Vote | `size_of::<Vote>()` plus the largest constituent signature length, bounding the single cloned signature backing at one time. The signature Vec descriptor is already inside Vote. |
| Body/preimage overlap | Fixed canonical-body backing plus fixed v2 preimage backing AND two separate `Vec<u8>` descriptors. Tests cross-check both lengths AND capacities against `Vote::canonical_body()` and the snapshot domain's `vote_preimage()`. |
| Admission/return slots (S) | Standalone ticket and its admission Result, present guard, admission enum, inner/outer return Results, and inventory value/Option return slots. Each enclosing slot includes its nested fields. Separate slots conservatively cover source/destination move overlap; this does not assert multiple certificate allocations or multiply-charge heap backing. |
| Verifier/return slots (part of S) | Local optional signer descriptor (no backing on borrowed revalidation), summary, core Result, borrowed unit Result, and Proposal/Vote verifier Result, including conservative transfer overlap. The summary already contains its optional signer descriptor. No returned certificate or signer-vector backing exists on this path. |
| Later local signing/serialization | OUTSIDE this envelope: signing, completed timeout signatures, encoded output, and their temporaries. Original-ticket confirmation still occurs before signing and again before consumption. |
| Engine ingestion/TC formation/application | OUTSIDE the preceding boundary: accumulator clones, TC formation and serialization are not claimed covered by it. The selected TC gets a separate admission/revalidation boundary using its actual capacities; no previous triggering Timeout guard proves the selected TC. |

The checked envelope is R + C + single-Vote/body/preimage component + S.
It conservatively sums the named owner slots across admission, revalidation,
and return phases rather than relying on compiler slot reuse. It is not a
stack-frame inventory. Verification temporaries are destroyed synchronously
before the private guard returns; no new retained proof, cache, owned
certificate result, or asynchronous allocator coverage is introduced.
Inherited key-provider/backend work, returned backend error-string backing,
allocator metadata/rounding, stack-frame layout, global engine/process memory,
and physical memory/RSS remain excluded. No RSS observation, fresh Miri run,
or independent security review is claimed.

`run422_f7_retained_qc_actual_capacity_boundary_and_relief` is a direct
admission-helper test, not a lowered-budget handler test. Both a genuinely
signed Timeout and a TC with genuine signed evidence are admitted exactly at
their calculated boundary. Enlarging a signature's actual capacity by ONE byte
without changing its contents makes the same calculation refuse at boundary
+ 1, before any QC-backend call. Assertions preserve all message contents,
serialized input, the enlarged capacity/control charge, and engine view,
epoch, lock, committed baseline, latch, accumulator count, block count,
retained-byte accounting, evidence-rejection count, and evictions. Relieving
capacity pressure admits the same input again with three constituent checks.

| TC | 7,605 | 7,844 | 2,799 | 536 | 18,784 / 18,785 |

These are component-calculation observations, not physical allocation/RSS
measurements. The earlier `Some(u64::MAX)` control is retained and explicitly

```diff
diff --git a/crates/qbind-consensus/src/basic_hotstuff_engine.rs b/crates/qbind-consensus/src/basic_hotstuff_engine.rs
index dd97cb3..6c37f46 100755
--- a/crates/qbind-consensus/src/basic_hotstuff_engine.rs
+++ b/crates/qbind-consensus/src/basic_hotstuff_engine.rs
@@ -5216,6 +5216,39 @@ pub mod received_qc_effect_test_support;
 #[cfg(test)]
 mod tests {
     use super::*;
+    #[test]
+    fn run422_timeout_view_exhaustion_baseline_characterization() {
+        let mut engine = BasicHotStuffEngine::<[u8; 32]>::new(
+            ValidatorId(1),
+            make_validator_set(1),
+        );
+        assert!(engine.try_advance_to_view(u64::MAX - 1));
+        let result = std::panic::catch_unwind(std::panic::AssertUnwindSafe(|| {
+            engine.on_timeout_msg(
+                ValidatorId(1),
+                TimeoutMsg::new(u64::MAX - 1, None, ValidatorId(1)),
+            )
+        }));
+        println!(
+            "baseline+test patch: debug_assertions={} search_panicked={} inserted={} result={:?}",
+            cfg!(debug_assertions), result.is_err(), engine.timeout_count(u64::MAX - 1), result
+        );
+        assert_eq!(engine.timeout_count(u64::MAX - 1), 1);
+        assert!(matches!(result, Err(_) | Ok(Ok(None))));
+        let tc = engine.timeout_accumulator().maybe_tc_for(
+            engine.state.validators(), u64::MAX - 1,
+        ).expect("eligible TC skipped or panic after insertion");
+        assert_eq!(tc.view, u64::MAX);
+
+        let mut accumulator = TimeoutAccumulator::<[u8; 32]>::new();
+        assert_eq!(accumulator.on_timeout(
+            engine.state.validators(), TimeoutMsg::new(u64::MAX, None, ValidatorId(1)),
+        ), Ok(true));
+        let invalid = accumulator.maybe_tc_for(engine.state.validators(), u64::MAX)
+            .expect("baseline forms terminal TC");
```

## RUN 422 — Native ordinary Transaction empty-auth refusal (F1 code/test remediation)

**Scope and call path.** This change is limited to `qbind_wire::tx::Transaction` on the native system-program route: `Node::apply_block` decodes each proposal blob and passes decoded transactions to `BlockExecutor`; `BlockExecutor` invokes `TxExecutor::execute_transaction`; that calls `ExecutionContext::verify_tx_auth`, which forwards to `verify_transaction_auth` (`crates/qbind-node/src/lib.rs:2595`, `crates/qbind-runtime/src/lib.rs:149,183`, `crates/qbind-ledger/src/context.rs:49-50`, `crates/qbind-ledger/src/auth.rs:25-34`). The verifier now returns `ExecutionError::InvalidCallData("transaction requires at least one authentication entry")` immediately for `auths.is_empty()`, before `tx_digest`, account-store access, signature-suite lookup or signature verification. Nonempty-auth verification behavior is unchanged.

This is the bounded minimum-authentication portion of F1 only. It does not enforce thresholds/weights, key deduplication, payer or required-signer coverage, account ownership policy, or full F2. It adds no empty-auth mode or genesis/field-based exception. `BlockExecutor` retains its existing sequential, per-transaction result semantics and does not roll back earlier/later successful effects. `Node::apply_block` can return a block outcome containing a failed transaction; the test does not claim that every transaction failure rejects the whole block. Existing transaction-count, malformed-blob and trailing-byte checks remain covered.

**Baseline characterization (separate from final validation).** At baseline commit `fa3e5c14e9e2a8f51d4365688cca8d8cba8778d1` / root tree `d415c31e3ad8dbd6d721dc4e26db59e1d543eccf`, `auth.rs` blob `bf20fa32497b09351aac78ab0448a34a8cce5292` returned `Ok(())` for an empty auth vector; the baseline test blob `4543b0b7de1f8129799c685511179030e27808a1` contains `verify_transaction_auth_empty_auths_succeeds`, which directly exercised that branch. In an isolated detached baseline worktree, the test-only selection

```text
LIBCLANG_PATH=/usr/lib/llvm-18/lib CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/workspaces/QBIND/olivexo28/QBIND/target cargo test --locked -p qbind-ledger --test tx_auth_verifier_tests verify_transaction_auth_empty_auths_succeeds -- --exact --nocapture
```

exited 0: 1 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored, 8 filtered out. This is source/test characterization only, not a reproduced deployed exploit or deployed-binary evidence.

**Acceptance evidence and source revision.** Tested Rust source is commit `b521de4fdbc8496dbffb0b125efb594e2d9ced81` (tree `b2dc348e1ed896f28f7d721305eee293ebeff8d4`); it is a direct child of the required baseline. ### RUN 422 bounded native required-signer coverage (2026-10-31)

**Baseline and scope.** The clean starting checkout was independently checked with `git status --porcelain=v1` (empty), `git remote -v` (fetch/push origin `https://github.com/olivexo28/QBIND`), `git rev-parse HEAD` (`d8cfe5061af76b1457c22bc9c942d35dafae0f58`), `git cat-file -t d8cfe5061af76b1457c22bc9c942d35dafae0f58` (`commit`), and separate baseline/HEAD `^{tree}` queries (both `a9cb05e2e509e598ee2ffeffe0f2bd10e729cf3f`). `git merge-base --is-ancestor <baseline> HEAD` exited 0: identity establishes the starting ancestry, not unavailable earlier history. `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` returned true and `.git/shallow` names the baseline; its empty visible parent list is a shallow boundary, not evidence of a historical root. Remote main initially matched the baseline; the requested task branch did not exist and was created locally. Delivery pushes only `copilot/run-422-native-required-signer-coverage`, without PR, main push, merge or force-push.

**Pre-fix characterization, not post-fix or deployed-path evidence.** A temporary test-only patch to `tx_auth_verifier_tests.rs`, with the pinned production verifier unchanged, generated two distinct ML-DSA-44 keypairs and authenticated both required indices. Removing one auth left a nonempty vector, the complete body and surviving signature unchanged; restoration reproduced the complete original transaction and both digests matched. The baseline verifier accepted both the complete and partial transaction. Literal command: `LIBCLANG_PATH=/usr/lib/llvm-18/lib cargo test --locked -p qbind-ledger --test tx_auth_verifier_tests baseline_nonempty_partial_authentication_characterization -- --nocapture`. First exit 101 was a missing-libclang build failure (no tests selected/executed; passed/failed/ignored not applicable), not a behavioral result. After installing missing `libclang-18-dev`, the identical command exited 0: 1 selected, 1 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored, 10 filtered out. The temporary characterization patch/logs were retained as session artifacts, not shipped as baseline behavior or production changes; the characterization-only test was replaced by final refusal assertions.

**Correction.** The existing exact empty-auth error, `InvalidCallData("transaction requires at least one authentication entry")`, still precedes all other checks, digest, store and crypto work. Nonempty preflight checks u16 account/auth counts first, then each auth's index range and signer mark in vector order, then coverage of all bit-0 required indices in account order. Fixed redacted messages are respectively `"transaction account count exceeds wire limit"`, `"transaction authentication count exceeds wire limit"`, `"auth.account_index out of range"`, `"authentication account is not a required signer"` and `"required signer authentication missing"`, all `InvalidCallData`. Work is O(accounts + auths), with an allocation-free 8192-byte bitmap derived from the existing u16 account-count limit. This bounds only coverage storage, not the entire verifier, stack frame, backend or physical memory. At most 65535 accounts means the highest usable index is 65534; u16 index 65535 is deterministically out of range. Exact-index coverage does not deduplicate account IDs or establish distinct-key/weighted authorization.

Every supplied auth still undergoes existing keyset lookup, suite selection and cryptographic verification after structural coverage; presence is not signature validity, and an invalid extra auth refuses. Wire encoding, TxSignBody/tx_digest, reserved fields, suite policy and key selection are untouched. Required signer declarations are transaction-supplied and signed: TxSignBody includes every account's ID, flags, access hint and reserved bytes; it excludes auths, permitting the unchanged-body removal test.

**Final acceptance evidence.** Genuine ML-DSA-44 positives cover two distinct required accounts and repeated IDs at different required indices. Nonempty removal and duplicate-first-auth cases cannot cover the other index; malformed/tampered signatures and a cryptographically invalid extra entry still refuse. Explicitly structural-only counting providers cover preflight ordering (zero store reads/writes/deletes, provider lookups and backend calls), count overflow, the maximum representable auth count, highest usable index, index 65535 refusal and writable-only accounts. Existing empty-auth, bad-index, missing-keyset and suite/signature controls remain effective. No mock-provider positive is cryptographic acceptance evidence.

Actual `TxExecutor`, sequential `BlockExecutor` and `Node::apply_block` tests remove one genuinely generated auth without altering the surviving signature or complete body. The exact failed-transaction error is `InvalidCallData("required signer authentication missing")`; refused-only runs compare the full backing account map (complete accounts, not balances alone) and record zero put/delete mutations. Mixed blocks retain that failure and two later successes; the last transaction genuinely authenticates using the keyset created by the preceding successful transaction. Complete final maps equal the valid-only sequential control. Node tests distinguish successful outer block application from failed transaction execution and compare the complete actual `BlockProposal`, including all transaction payload bytes, before/after both refused-only and mixed application. These are in-process native harness paths, not ingress/deployment assurance; node consensus suite 1 remains an explicitly structural harness control.

The legacy node keyset-create fixture marked the not-yet-created target `flags=3` although only the separate existing authorizing keyset was authenticated. That inconsistency is corrected to target `flags=2` (writable-only), matching the runtime fixtures. The existing authorizing keyset remains `flags=1` and genuinely authenticated; changed bodies are signed afresh. No genuine signer requirement was cleared.

**Tested source identity.** Rust source revision `6130b703f1d2af42ddf8c2daddb2f234a13a8d52`, root tree `321f3e5615561745092ed771d574fc3b56e7433f`. Final Rust validation is attributed only to this revision, not the baseline characterization or previous runs:
